title: Normal release starts from the version PR merge push
context: The production release workflow ran on the version PR's `pull_request` closed event. That run's ref is the PR merge ref, which the main-only production QA environment rejects, and it was rejected only after the candidate had been promoted. v0.17.0 was left live without acceptance until an owner dispatch finished it.
decision: A normal release starts from the `push` to `main` that merges the version PR. The run looks up the merged pull request for the pushed commit through the GitHub API and authorizes it with the same validation as an owner retry. It proceeds only when the release owner made the merge. A push that merged a pull request from another branch or repository ends without releasing, and an unresolved or ambiguous lookup fails. An owner dispatch remains the retry path.

alternatives.reason: Its run executes on the PR merge ref, so the main-only production QA environment rejects it after promotion.

alternatives.option: Allow other refs in the production QA environment
alternatives.reason: Any branch's workflow could then request the protected environment, weakening the gate the release depends on.

alternatives.option: Start every release by owner dispatch
alternatives.reason: It adds a manual step after the merge that already expresses the authorization.

alternatives.option: Identify the version PR from the merge commit message
alternatives.reason: A commit message can be forged; the merged pull request record cannot.

consequences: The release run's ref is `main`, so the production QA environment admits it.
A merge by anyone other than the release owner fails closed; the owner then dispatches a retry.
Recovery accepts original runs started by `push` or owner dispatch.
The push path needs no ancestry check: the controller is the pushed commit's first parent, the trusted main before the merge.
revisitTriggers: GitHub evaluates environment branch policies for `pull_request` runs against the base branch.
Releases need to start from something other than a merge to `main`.
